predecessors.name: Kharijite imamate of Ifriqiya
predecessors.text: Tahert (Tagdemt), where Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam founded a Kharijite principality in 761 after the Abbasids retook Ifriqiya

successors.name: Fatimid Caliphate
successors.text: Tahert and the area surrounding it, conquered by the Fatimids in 909; the last imam fled to Ouargla

rulers.name: Yusuf Abu Hatim ibn Muhammad (second reign)
rulers.title: Imam

ledger.x: 777: Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam is elected Ibadi imam at Tahert.

812: after the Huwara's siege of Tripoli ('In 812, Imam Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Rahman supported the Huwara in their siege of Tripoli, which was held by the Aghlabids') the Aghlabid emir Abdallah ibn Ibrahim 'made peace with the Rustamids by ceding Tripolitania'.
By the 880s (dated 880): 'However, its area contracted to Tahert and the area surrounding it by the 880s.'

3 or 4 May 896: the Aghlabid emir Ibrahim II defeats the Nafusa, led by the Rustamid governor Aflah ibn al-Abbas, near the fort of Manu; 'The disaster at Manu marked the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa'.
909: the Rustamid imamate ends with the fall of Tahert; Cliopatria's last year is 910.

wars.name: Idrisid attack on Tahert (Battle of Tahert)
wars.outcome: The Idrisids attacked the Rustamids at Tahert in 789 or 790; the page gives no result and no change of land.

wars.name: Rustamid-Aghlabid conflict over Tripoli
wars.outcome: In 812 the imam Abd al-Wahhab backed the Huwara in their siege of Tripoli, which the Aghlabids held; the two sides reached a modus vivendi, which displeased Ibadi tribes on the Aghlabid border who 'launched a few rebellions'; then 'Aghlabid Emir Abdallah ibn…

wars.name: Aghlabid campaign against the Nafusa (Battle of Manu)
wars.outcome: 3 or 4 May 896 near the fort of Manu: Aghlabid victory over the Nafusa under the Rustamid governor Aflah ibn al-Abbas, 'the end of Rustamid rule over Jebal Nafusa'; Aghlabid raids on Qantrara (near Nefta) and, in August-September 897, on the Nafusa again.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Tahert
wars.outcome: The Fatimids conquer Tahert in 909; the last imam and many Ibadis flee to Ouargla, sheltered by the Sedrata.

certainty.note: The page names no frontier; the Saharan edge, the Tlemcen frontier and the Tunisian reach are approximate.
As before; the Jebel Nafusa part rests on the 812 cession and the Battle of Manu page, and the page does not say how much of Tripolitania was ceded.
Tahert and 150 km around it is my reading of 'the area surrounding it'.
